+
+## The sub-agent loop
+
+`agent.Loop` runs one sub-agent over the single-prompt model gateway, so it
+works with any provider. Each turn the model returns one JSON object: a tool
+call, or its findings. The loop runs the tool and replays the whole transcript
+on the next turn.
+
+- **Metered.** `agent.Model` reserves the worst case before every call (input
+  estimated at three bytes per token, which errs high), waits when other
+  in-flight calls hold the headroom, and settles real usage with cached input
+  priced separately. A failed call is settled at its input size with no output,
+  so a provider that bills incomplete requests is not ignored. `Spend().Overruns`
+  counts calls whose real input exceeded the estimate.
+- **Results are data.** Each step is JSON inside an `<untrusted_tool_step>`
+  tag, so a file containing `</untrusted_tool_step>` cannot close it.
+- **Errors go back to the model.** A bad path, unknown tool, or invalid
+  arguments becomes a failed step the model can correct. Tool errors never
+  include git's stderr or local paths.
+- **Bounded.** The tool-call limit is announced when reached ("You cannot call
+  more tools"); a model that still asks for tools fails the task with
+  `ErrToolCallLimit`. When the transcript outgrows 120 KiB, the oldest results
+  are replaced by a marker and the model is asked for its findings.
+- **Tolerant of imperfect output, strict about what ships.** Replies may be
+  wrapped in a code fence or prose, and one invalid reply gets a repair note.
+  Findings are validated one by one: unknown fields are ignored and severity
+  case is normalized, but a finding that still fails `Validate` is dropped and
+  recorded as a `dropped_finding` trace note with the reason, instead of
+  rejecting the whole answer.
+
+Because the transcript is replayed every turn, input tokens grow with each tool
+call. A sub-agent that makes twelve calls can read a large multiple of its
+final transcript, which is why input tokens are the budget most likely to run
+out first.

explanations.title: Usage accounting exposes overruns
explanations.summary: Spend now reports reservation overruns, while model usage pricing can apply a separate rate to cached input tokens. This makes underestimates and cached-input costs visible in accounting.

explanations.title: Sub-agents can use tools
explanations.summary: Sub-agents now take turns returning either a tool call or findings. Each tool result is added to the transcript for the next model call, allowing the agent to inspect code before reporting.

explanations.title: One malformed reply is recoverable
explanations.summary: An unusable model reply gets one repair prompt; a second consecutive unusable reply ends the task. This lets the loop recover from a malformed response without retrying indefinitely.

explanations.title: Tool errors can be corrected
explanations.summary: Tool failures are recorded as failed steps and shown to the model instead of ending the run, so it can correct a path or try a different tool. The displayed error comes from the tool rather than git stderr or local paths.

explanations.title: Dropped findings are auditable
explanations.summary: Each discarded finding is recorded in the review trace with its title and reason, making the filtering visible rather than silent.

explanations.title: Tool history and calls are bounded
explanations.summary: When the transcript exceeds its byte limit, older tool results are replaced with omission markers and the model is asked to finish. The loop also stops accepting tool requests at the configured call limit and fails if the model keeps requesting tools.

explanations.title: Model calls are metered
explanations.summary: Model calls reserve budget using an input estimate and the maximum output allowance, waiting when other in-flight calls temporarily hold the available budget. Actual usage is settled afterward; failed calls are accounted at the input estimate with no output.

explanations.title: Invalid findings no longer discard valid ones
explanations.summary: Findings are validated individually, so a malformed finding no longer discards valid findings in the same response. Severity and type casing are normalized, unknown fields are tolerated, and invalid or over-limit findings are reported as drops.

explanations.title: Traces support audit notes
explanations.summary: Review traces now accept note events, allowing non-tool and non-model events such as discarded findings to be included in the trace.
